title: See the shape of the data without leaving the CLI
description: Textplot renders ASCII and Unicode charts as `VARCHAR` values right inside a `SELECT`. The point: when you're poking at data in the [DuckDB CLI](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/cli/overview), you can see the shape of a distribution, the trend of a series, or the level of a metric without copying numbers into a notebook or a BI tool. Quick eyeballing — not a replacement for real visualization when you actually need axes, hover, or pixels.

sections.title: What it is
sections.description: Inline visuals for terminal-first SQL workflows. When you're at a DuckDB prompt staring at a column of numbers, the usual way to understand its shape is to leave SQL — copy the values into a notebook, draw a chart, come back. Textplot removes that detour: a distribution, a per-entity trend, or a status level becomes a chart you read directly in the result table. It pairs naturally with [`fuzzycomplete`](/products/extensions/fuzzycomplete) as the two extensions worth installing for an "I live in the REPL" workflow — one makes typing queries painless, the other makes reading their output painless.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Every function returns a single `VARCHAR`. That is the entire architecture, and it is the load-bearing design choice: there is no client-side renderer, no asset pipeline, no extra dependency in the query plan. A chart is just another string column, so the glyphs travel anywhere a text column can go.

bulletPoints.label: Charts are plain text
bulletPoints.description: Because the output is a `VARCHAR`, a generated chart composes with [`.mode line`](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/cli/output_formats), `.mode markdown`, log redirection, `tee` to a file, a status email, or a README paste — exactly like any other string column, with no rendering step in between.

bulletPoints.label: Fixed-width alignment
bulletPoints.description: Width is a parameter, so charts line up cleanly column-over-column across rows in a result table — which is what makes per-row sparklines and bars readable as a fleet view.

sections.title: What it isn't
sections.description: Textplot is a CLI ergonomics tool. It earns its place when the alternative is squinting at numbers — not when you actually need a real chart.

bulletPoints.label: Not a visualization library
bulletPoints.description: Character-grid resolution caps detail. For interactive dashboards, publication figures, or anything where pixels matter, use a real charting tool — [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org/), [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/), [Observable Plot](https://observablehq.com/plot), [Apache Superset](https://superset.apache.org/), etc.

bulletPoints.label: Not a statistical summary
bulletPoints.description: A density plot shows the shape of a distribution; it doesn't compute moments, fit kernels, or give you confidence intervals. Pair it with `quantile_cont`, `stddev_pop`, or [`datasketches`](/products/extensions/datasketches) when you need numbers.

bulletPoints.label: Unicode rendering varies
bulletPoints.description: Emoji and block characters depend on the terminal font, so the same chart can look different across environments. For maximum portability, fall back to the ASCII styles or supply your own characters.
